items.title: 52031_Kenny Clarke oral history interview
items.q: Sometimes Joe would just say, "Well, I'm not working tonight. Kenny take my place."

ctx.x: But what happened -- and Basie, we've been tight for about 35 years. I used to just get on his bus and go everywhere. I don't care where -- I'd say, "Where you going, Base?" He'd say, "I'm going to so and so." Okay, I'm going too. I'd just get on the bus and go. Like Freddie and Basie would see that I had something to eat and a place to stay, so I never worried. Sometimes Joe would just say, "Well, I'm not working tonight. Kenny take my place." And I used to play with Basie all the time.

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I used to give my Kenny my key to the Y.

ctx.x: Yeh, amateur drummer, he would review the records and he wasn't in the studio and he said, "Jo Jones," and I said, "George, I wasn't there; that was Kenny Clarke." But Kenny would do what we were trying to do. We were trying to do something to bring these kids along and to try to help them, because we were already established and we already had a job, but who were we going to get for a replacement. Because you remember, Milt, in show business years ago when you got to be around 35 or 40 years old you stayed at…

drunk Wednesday like you did last Wednesday. You better be on your job. Because you know good and well that Sid Catlett will come around and if you did anything wrong, we just get up and take your job."
